full_judgment:
Mr. D. M. Ansaruddin Ahmed, J.:- This Rule arises out of an application under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and is directed against the judgment and order passed on 30.11.92 by the District Judge, Comilla in Election Tribunal Appeal No. 2 of 1992 affirming those passed on 16.7.92 by the Senior Assistant Judge. Additional Court and Election Tribunal No. 2, Comilla Sadar, allowing the Election Tribunal Case No. 6 of 1992. 

 2. Opposite party No. 1 Shamsuddin Patwari filed the above mentioned Election Tribunal Case under Section 16 of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Ordinance 1983, hereinafter referred to as the Ordinance, read with Rule 44 of the Union Parishad (Election) Rules 1983 against the petitioner Md. Nazimuddin Chowdhury for setting aside the election of the petitioner as chairman of No. 13 Adra Union Parishad under P. S Barura, District Comilla. 

 3. Briefly stated, the election petitioner's case was that he filed nomination paper within time for election to the post of chairman of the union parishad but he was disqualified by the Returning Officer on 8.12.91 on the ground that he was a teacher of Ekbaria Senior Madrasah receiving contribution from the Government towards salary, and as a result the petitioner declared elected uncontested. His appeal of the Upazila Nirbahi Officer was dismissed. Writ Petition No 3267 of 1991 filed by him was also dismissed with the observation that his remedy lay before the Election Tribunal, it was contended that he was a teacher of a Private Madrasah and that having not held any office of profit in the service of the Republic or of the Union Parishad or any other local authority he was illegally disqualified and the respondent was illegally declared elected, chair-man' of the Union Parishad. 

 4. The respondent contested the case contending inter alia that the election petitioner’s nomination paper was validly rejected, as receiving Government contribution as part of his salary he was holding office of profit in the service of local authority. 

 5. Only the contesting parties examined themselves in the case and the learned Election Tribunal on consideration of the evidence on records held that the election petitioners was illegally declared disqualified and the respondent was declared illegally elected. The Tribunal allowed the case and declared the respondent's election void. Against the judgment and order of the Election Tribunal the respondent preferred and appeal before the learned District Judge, relying upon the decision 2BLT (HCD) 1994 Md. N. Chowdhury Vs. S. Patwari & Ors. (D. M. Ansiruddin Ahmed, .1) .9 in the case of Maulana Abdul Haque V. S. Fazlul Huq and others reported in B. C. R. 1987 (HCD) 198 the learned Judge has concurred with the Tribunal holding that the rejection of the nomination paper of the election petitioner has been illegal. He has accordingly dismissed the appeal. Against this appellate decision the returned candidate has obtained the instant Rule. 

 7. Mr. A. K. Badrul Haque, learned Advocate for the opposite party on the other hand support the impugned judgment and order and submits that receipt of Government contribution by a teacher of a private Madrasah does not make him a person holding office of profit in the service of any local authority or even of the Republic. He contends that the petitioner has even not disclosed as to who is the' local authority under which the opposite party was serving at the time when the nomination paper was submitted. Mr. Huq maintains that the Court below has rightly relied upon the decision reported in B. C. R 1987 (HCD) 198 in holding that the election petitioner's eligibility to contest the election as chairman of Union Parishad cannot be questioned. He submits that opposite party a teacher of Private Madrasah holds office in the service of neither the Republic on any local authority and the Government contribution towards a percentage of his salary does not being his case within the mischief of provision of Section 7(2)(e) of the Ordinance. 

 8. There is no dispute that the opposite party filed nomination appear for con-testing the election to the post of Chairman of No. 13 Adra Union Parishad under P. S Barura in time and that the nomination paper was rejected on the ground that being Madrasah teacher receiving 70% of his salary as contribution from Government Exchequer, he asked disqualification under Section 7(2)(e) of the Ordinance, which provides that a person shall be disqualified for election or nomination as or for being a Chairman or member if he holds any full time office of profit in the Service of the Republic or of the Union Parishad or of any other local authority. The , petitioner who was declared elected uncontested appears to have taken a defence that the election petitioner was holding office of profit in the service of the local authority, but it has been kept vague throughout as to who was the local authority either the Madrasah or Union Parishad or Zilla Parishad. "Local Authority" has, been defined in Section 3(28) of the General Clauses Act and it means and includes the pourashava Zilla Board, Union Panchayet. Board of Trustee of a port or other authority legally entitled to a entrusted by the Government with, the control or management of a municipal or local fund or any corporation or others body or authority constituted or established by the Government under any law. The terms implies a public duty authorised by law or by the Government to carry on some administrative function, it is not the defendant's case that Union Parishad or Zilla Parishad or any other local authority or body has any concern with the administration of the Madrasah or can it be said that the private institution itself is the local authority defined as above. Mere receipt of the Government contribution by a teacher of a private institution does not imply that he holds the post in the service of any local authority nor is it a service of the Republic as defined in Article 152 of the Constitution. In the case relied upon the court below the petitioner a vice-principal of a Private Madrasah was held to be eligible to contest the election as chairman of a Union Parishad. Respectfully agreeing with the view taken in that case I do hold that a teacher of a Private Madrasah receiving a part of his salary as contribution from the Government does not hold office of profit in the service of the Republic or any local authority and as such does not earn any disqualification within the meaning of Section 7(2)(e) of the Ordinance. I agree with the court below that the Returning Officer and for the matter of that his appellate body have acted illegally in rejecting the nomination paper submitted by the election petitioner (Opposite party herein).
